repos.name: cursor/plugins
repos.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins
repos.eli5: It's like a toolbox of add‑ons that let the Cursor coding helper work with other programs, just like adding new apps to your phone. Developers who use Cursor install these to get extra features.

repos.name: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
repos.description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/
repos.eli5: Imagine a universal remote that can control any software, letting AI helpers talk to programs as easily as pressing a button. Programmers and AI agents use it to run any command‑line tool.

repos.name: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
repos.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
repos.eli5: It’s like a super‑fast research assistant that reads the internet for the past month and writes a simple summary, so anyone can get the latest info without searching themselves.

repos.name: getarcaneapp/arcane
repos.description: Modern Docker Management, Designed for Everyone
repos.eli5: Think of it as a friendly dashboard that lets you start, stop, and watch Docker containers the way you’d control toys on a play mat. Sysadmins and developers use it to manage apps.

repos.name: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
repos.description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills and plugins with quality gates, security scanning, harness compatibility checks, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior. Ships reusable CI templates that bring every check to any repository.
repos.eli5: It works like a report card for AI add‑ons, checking they’re safe, work well together, and actually improve the AI’s job before they’re released. AI developers use it to test their plugins.

repos.name: nvm-sh/nvm
repos.description: Node Version Manager - POSIX-compliant bash script to manage multiple active node.js versions.
repos.eli5: It’s a shelf that holds many versions of Node.js so you can pick the right one for each project, just like swapping books on a shelf. JavaScript developers use it to manage Node versions.

repos.name: astral-sh/uv
repos.description: An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.
repos.eli5: Imagine a super‑speedy kitchen robot that prepares all your Python ingredients, builds the dish, and cleans up, faster than any other tool. Python programmers use it to install packages and manage projects.

repos.name: google-research/paper-orchestra
repos.description: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
repos.eli5: It’s like a band of robot writers that each play a part—outline, research, drawing graphs—to turn raw ideas into a finished research paper, just like musicians creating a song together. Researchers use it to draft papers automatically.

repos.name: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
repos.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
repos.eli5: Think of it as a set of LEGO pieces that let coding robots build and fix software, fitting together easily with the Stitch platform. Developers using Stitch add these skills to their AI assistants.

repos.name: sveltejs/svelte
repos.description: web development for the rest of us
repos.eli5: It’s like a magic pen that lets you draw a website, and it automatically turns your sketch into fast, clean code. Web developers use it to build interactive sites easily.
